attack.failure: Treating intact H and impact-driven pins as indispensable overlooks the expressly supported sleeve-and-stem retention operation. Removing that dependency does not remove setup time, component occupancy, or release work.
attack.invariant: The same two aligned panels retain at least 4 units at ticks 3 through 6 and separate with all installed retainers removed by boundary 10, without damage, discard, substitution, or outside resources.
attack.permitted_variable: Counterfactual branch forbids tap and hence reliance on intact H during fastening; detach, sleeve installation, stem insertion, withdrawal, removal, and restoration remain permitted. The hard retention function is unchanged.

budget_used.allocation: Declared before candidate search: six local concern passes, one slot each for identifying the presumed prerequisite, constructing one replacement, timing, resource occupancy, burden comparison, and uncertainty/failure closure. Candidate cap three; only one construction pursued; no fresh builder.
budget_used.limits: One bounded native role; six local concern passes are not independent agents. The 1800-word cap is not equal compute.

candidates.burden: Six operator actions, including restoring H, plus idle ticks 3 through 6. Five actions suffice for retention and release alone. The stem is occupied in V from boundary 3 until boundary 8; H is unavailable intact from boundary 1 until boundary 10. Compared with the archived two-pin route, this replaces two impacts and two pulls with five setup/release operations plus restoration; compared with clip fastening it increases operator work from two actions to six. It spends zero taps but is not a demonstrated labor improvement.
candidates.defeat: No supported opening remains if detached/free S cannot be obtained or V is unavailable: this construction then fails, and N05 authorizes no invented replacement or altered capacity. In the stipulated case the timing margin before retention starts is zero: delaying any of its consecutive setup actions beyond ticks 0, 1, 2 misses boundary 3. With the chosen release schedule, delaying the final restoration misses its additional boundary-10 restoration goal; required separation itself is complete at boundary 9.
candidates.lineage: Initial construction from this literal packet under N05; no received candidates, historical files, or other method.
candidates.mechanism: Forbid intact-H impact fastening. Detach H to make S free, install V, and insert S into V. Their stipulated joint capacity is min(4,4)=4, independent of pins and impacts. Withdraw S before removing V to eliminate the installed assembly; reassemble free M and S afterward. Replacement dependencies are a detachable H, free S, available V, three consecutive initial operator slots, the supported sleeve-stem relationship, ordered withdrawal/removal, and one final slot plus free M and S for restoration.
candidates.prediction: Modeled, not measured: detach completes at boundary 1; V installation completes at 2 and alone creates no stated retention; insertion completes at 3, supplying 4 units through boundary 7 and until withdrawal completes at 8. V removal completes at 9, leaving the panels released and no installed retainer. H restoration completes at 10. Zero taps. No use or assumption of Q_theta.

handoff.residue: The intact hammer is unavailable throughout the hold interval, and the stem cannot serve elsewhere while installed. Zero impact is bought with extra operator work and no setup slack. Restoration is additional to the panel-release requirement.
handoff.summary: Replay exactly detach(H) at 0, install(V) at 1, insert(S,V) at 2, withdraw(S,V) at 7, remove(V) at 8, assemble(H) at 9; unspecified ticks idle. Keep one operator, next-boundary completion, exclusive resource occupancy, no pins alongside the sleeve assembly, and unchanged 4-unit hold at ticks 3-6 and all-retainers-removed separation by boundary 10. This N05 branch forbids intact-H impact fastening but permits H disassembly. Rely only on J06 capacity, not Q or outside physics. Refuse the construction if S or V is unavailable or the setup misses boundary 3. Treat all outcomes as stipulated-model predictions for root replay.

limits: This is one candidate proposal, not a replay result, independent review, measured performance, or final self-grade.
The case is a stipulated finite model; sleeve retention gives no claim about empirical friction, geometry, durability, or safety.
The ordinary two-pin and clip constructions are already archived. This proposal makes no global novelty or superiority claim.
No changed mechanical law, capacity, demand, deadline, extra staff, or outside operation is used. No impact-budget ladder cell is set; zero taps is a property of the proposed schedule.
AM and AI were supplied but are not used as source support; their synthetic analogues do not establish sleeve mechanics or replacement resources.
Q_theta remains unknown and is irrelevant to this construction; no favorable value is assumed.
